enhanced.fullText:
The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), codified at 29 U.S.C. §§ 201-219, establishes fundamental labor standards affecting higher education institutions nationwide. Originally enacted in 1938 and significantly amended in 1985 to include public sector employees, the FLSA governs minimum wage, overtime compensation, recordkeeping, and child labor standards for covered employees.

Under 29 U.S.C. § 206, universities must pay all non-exempt employees the federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour, unless state law requires a higher amount. The Act's overtime provisions, found in 29 U.S.C. § 207, mandate time-and-a-half compensation for non-exempt employees working more than 40 hours per workweek. Higher education institutions must carefully classify employees as exempt or non-exempt under the administrative, executive, professional, and learned professional exemptions detailed in 29 CFR Part 541.

The FLSA's recordkeeping requirements, specified in 29 U.S.C. § 211(c) and 29 CFR § 516.2, mandate universities preserve payroll records, collective bargaining agreements, and employee contracts for three years from the last date of entry. Basic employment records, wage rate tables, and records of wage additions or deductions must be retained for two years under 29 CFR § 516.5.

Section 7(r) of the FLSA, added by the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, requires employers provide reasonable break time and private space for nursing mothers to express breast milk for one year after childbirth. Universities must ensure compliance across all campus locations and employment classifications.

Enforcement authority rests with the Department of Labor's Wage and Hour Division under 29 U.S.C. § 211. Violations may result in back wages, liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages, and civil monetary penalties up to $2,374 per violation under 29 CFR § 578.3. Willful violations carry criminal penalties including fines up to $10,000 and imprisonment.

Recent regulatory updates include the 2019 overtime rule raising the salary threshold for exempt employees to $35,568 annually, significantly impacting university staff classifications and compensation structures.
enhanced.summary: The FLSA establishes minimum wage, overtime, and recordkeeping requirements for university employees. Universities must properly classify exempt/non-exempt staff, maintain detailed employment records, and provide nursing mother accommodations while ensuring compliance with federal wage standards.
enhanced.requirements:
## Wage and Hour Compliance
- Pay federal minimum wage of $7.25/hour to all non-exempt employees per 29 U.S.C. § 206
- Provide overtime compensation at 1.5x regular rate for hours exceeding 40 per workweek under 29 U.S.C. § 207
- Properly classify employees using exemption criteria in 29 CFR Part 541

## Recordkeeping Obligations
- Maintain payroll records and collective bargaining agreements for 3 years per 29 CFR § 516.2
- Preserve basic employment records and wage rate tables for 2 years under 29 CFR § 516.5
- Document all wage additions, deductions, and time records

## Nursing Mother Support
- Provide reasonable break time for milk expression per 29 U.S.C. § 207(r)
- Designate private, non-bathroom space for nursing mothers
- Ensure accommodations available for one year post-childbirth

## Compliance Monitoring
- Conduct regular audits of employee classifications
- Review compensation practices for FLSA compliance
- Train HR staff on current wage and hour requirements
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No routine federal reporting required under FLSA. Universities must respond to Department of Labor investigations within specified timeframes and maintain records available for inspection. Event-triggered obligations include reporting workplace injuries affecting wage calculations and documenting any overtime exemption determinations for audit purposes.
